home.hero.heading: Hands-on technical leadership for software teams under change.
home.hero.lead: I join product teams as a Technical Lead or Solutions Architect to modernise architecture, improve delivery reliability, and introduce AI workflows that remain reviewable and owned by the team.
home.hero.supporting: Inside the work. Sharper delivery. AI with judgment.

home.profileCard.meta3: close to the people building the product

home.situations.heading: Bring me in when
home.situations.momentum.title: A critical modernisation is losing momentum
home.situations.momentum.body: The architecture is becoming harder to change, business logic is duplicated, releases are risky, or the team is trapped between old and new systems.
home.situations.strategy.title: Strategy is not surviving contact with delivery
home.situations.strategy.body: Leadership intent is clear in meetings, but ownership, priorities, planning, reviews, and technical decisions pull in different directions.
home.situations.ai.title: AI experiments need to become dependable work
home.situations.ai.body: The team has tools or pilots, but lacks governed access, useful context, review points, repeatable workflows, or clear ownership.
home.help.heading: How I help
home.help.lead: Most engagements combine two of these. The mix follows the problem in front of the team, not a fixed package.
home.help.architecture.title: Architecture and safer change
home.help.architecture.body: I clarify boundaries and ownership, reduce duplicated business logic, improve testability, observability, and recovery, and make releases and future changes safer.
home.help.leadership.title: Embedded technical leadership
home.help.leadership.body: I make decisions with the team, align architecture, product priorities, and delivery, mentor engineers and improve review quality, and keep leadership intent connected to implementation.
home.help.aiWorkflows.title: AI-enabled engineering workflows
home.help.aiWorkflows.body: I identify work that benefits from assistants or agents, connect tools to approved systems with controlled access, add deterministic checks and human review, and build practices the team can understand and own.

home.principles.heading: How I work
home.principles.1: Embedded closely enough to understand the actual constraints.
home.principles.2: Direct with sponsors and respectful of the people doing the work.
home.principles.3: Hands-on with architecture, code, reviews, and delivery.
home.principles.4: Pragmatic about Agile and AI: use what improves the system, discard what does not.
home.principles.5: Focused on leaving clearer ownership and stronger capability behind.
home.principles.closing.label: what this is not /
home.principles.closing: No transformation theatre, detached slideware, or AI adoption for its own sake.
home.questions.heading: Questions I get asked
home.questions.ai.q: How do you use AI in client work?
home.questions.ai.a: Only within the client's approved security and data-handling constraints. I separate client environments, control tool access, keep important actions reviewable, and use deterministic checks around model output. AI supports engineering judgment; it does not replace accountability.
home.questions.handsOn.a: Yes. The work includes architecture, code, reviews, debugging, delivery practices, mentoring, and stakeholder alignment. I am most useful where technical decisions and team execution need to improve together.
home.questions.partTime.a: Yes. Embedded engagements can be structured from two to five days per week when responsibilities, meeting cadence, and response expectations are explicit.
home.questions.onsite.a: I am based in Munich and work remotely across DACH, with planned onsite work where it materially improves the engagement.

work.about.heading: About me
work.about.p1: Across 20 engagements, the useful work was rarely only technical or only organizational. Delivery improved when code, ownership, feedback, and trust were handled together.
work.about.p2: I work close to teams that build the product, help make decisions explicit, and support sponsors who want faster delivery without more theater.

work.section.cleanAgile.heading: Architecture and safer change
work.section.cleanAgile.p: Boundaries, state, tests, and architecture that let teams change software without creating a new knot every sprint.
work.section.learner.heading: Alignment, incentives, and ownership
work.section.learner.p: Clearer reviews, smaller slices, visible trade-offs, and enough trust between sponsors, middle layers, and teams for change to survive daily pressure.
work.section.automation.heading: AI adoption with judgment
work.section.automation.p: Assistants, agents, and automation where the work is clear enough to describe, review, and own. If the process is vague, I fix that before adding AI.
